records.title: Finger millet (ragi)
records.summary: A hardy small-grained cereal traditionally grown on poor red and lateritic soils; tolerates acidic, low-fertility ground and stores very well.
instructions: Sow in pits or beds after reliable rains; thin to the strongest few plants per spot.
Good partner with a legume such as cowpea or horse gram in alternate rows or pits.
everyday_amounts: a pinch of a few seeds per planting spot
sow about one finger-joint deep
limitations: No yield is promised; poor soil and short rains limit harvests.
Ripens unevenly; needs two pickings.
safety_notes: Check seed is not chemically treated before eating any of it.
records.name: Finger millet

cautions.reason: Needs roughly three to four months; too long to finish if the rains are already ending.
Longer than the other millets; risky if the season length is not known.
If rains are well under way, a long crop may run into the dry period.

records.water_needs_plain: Moderate. Copes with short dry spells once established but needs moist soil at sowing and at flowering.
records.rooting_notes: Dense, shallow, fibrous roots: well suited to a hand's depth of soil in pits and beds.
records.maturity_description: About three to four months from sowing; quicker local types finish sooner. Heads ripen unevenly.
why_it_may_fit: Traditionally grown on lateritic and red soils
Grain stores for a long time

records.title: Pearl millet (bajra)
records.summary: A very drought- and heat-hardy cereal that grows on poor, shallow, sandy or gravelly soils with low rainfall.
instructions: Sow a few seeds per pit after reliable rains; thin to the two or three strongest.
Birds attack ripening heads: plan to guard or cover heads near harvest.
everyday_amounts: a pinch of a few seeds per planting spot
sow about one finger-joint deep
limitations: Less tolerant of strong acidity than finger millet; watch trial plants for pale, stunted growth.
No yield is promised.
safety_notes: Check seed is not chemically treated before eating any of it.
records.name: Pearl millet

cautions.reason: Does not like waterlogged ground; plant only on raised beds where water pools.
Water sitting on the hard layer can rot roots; prefer raised beds.
Even a short crop is risky if the rains are already ending.

records.water_needs_plain: Low. Among the most drought-tolerant cereals, but sensitive to drought at flowering and grain filling.
records.rooting_notes: Roots grow fast and spread widely; tolerates shallow soils better than maize or sorghum.
records.maturity_description: About ten to thirteen weeks from sowing for early types.
why_it_may_fit: Short season fits a short wet season
Copes with low fertility and shallow soil

records.title: Little millet (samai)
records.summary: A small, quick millet grown by hill and tribal farmers on poor, gravelly soils; one of the fastest grains to finish.
instructions: Broadcast thinly or sow a pinch per spot in beds; thin to avoid crowding.
everyday_amounts: a pinch of a few seeds per planting spot
sow about one finger-joint deep
limitations: Seed can be hard to find; ask locally.
Small grain needs patient threshing and cleaning.
Suitability on this exact soil needs a local trial.
safety_notes: Check seed is not chemically treated before eating any of it.
records.name: Little millet

cautions.reason: Prefers drained ground; use raised beds where water pools.

records.water_needs_plain: Low to moderate. Tolerates dry spells and short seasons.
records.rooting_notes: Fine, shallow roots: suits thin soil in pits and beds.
records.maturity_description: Roughly ten to thirteen weeks from sowing for most local types.
why_it_may_fit: Useful when the rain window is uncertain

records.title: Cowpea (lobia)
records.summary: A fast, drought-hardy legume that copes with acidic, poor soils, feeds the soil with nitrogen, and gives leaves and pods as food.
instructions: Sow two or three seeds per spot after reliable rains; thin to the strongest one or two.
Pick young leaves sparingly for food once plants are well established.
everyday_amounts: a pinch of a few seeds per planting spot
sow about one finger-joint deep
limitations: Aphids and pod borers are common; check plants often.
No yield is promised.
safety_notes: Cook dry beans thoroughly.
Check seed is not chemically treated before eating any of it.
records.name: Cowpea

cautions.reason: Sensitive to waterlogging; use raised beds where water pools.
Roots rot if water sits on the hard layer.

records.water_needs_plain: Low to moderate. Tolerates dry spells; needs moisture at flowering and pod filling.
records.rooting_notes: Taproot with spreading side roots; manages in shallow beds and pits.
records.maturity_description: About nine to thirteen weeks for grain from early types; young leaves can be picked earlier.

records.title: Horse gram (kulthi)
records.summary: A very hardy legume traditionally grown on poor lateritic and gravelly soils with little rain; often sown later in the season.
instructions: Sow in pits or beds; it is often sown later in the rains to finish on the moisture left in the soil.
Keep weeds down in the first weeks.
everyday_amounts: a pinch of a few seeds per planting spot
sow about one finger-joint deep
limitations: Heavy rain early can harm young plants.
No yield is promised.
safety_notes: Cook seed thoroughly before eating.
records.name: Horse gram

cautions.reason: Does not tolerate waterlogging; flooded ground will kill it.
Keep it out of spots where water stands; use raised spots.
Heavy rain on poorly drained ground harms young plants.

records.water_needs_plain: Very low. One of the most drought-tolerant pulses; can finish on stored soil moisture.
records.rooting_notes: Deep taproot where soil allows, but it is widely grown on shallow gravelly ground.
records.maturity_description: Roughly three to four months from sowing; early types are quicker.
why_it_may_fit: Traditionally grown on poor lateritic soils

records.title: Niger (ramtil)
records.summary: An oilseed grown by hill farmers on poor, acidic, shallow soils with little care; flowers attract bees.
instructions: Sow thinly in beds or along the edges of pits; seed is tiny, cover very lightly.
everyday_amounts: a pinch of seed per spot, barely covered
limitations: Seed may be hard to find; oil extraction needs crushing.
Suitability needs a local trial.
records.name: Niger

cautions.reason: Needs about three to four months; risky late in the rains.
Not a short crop; risky when the season length is unknown.

records.water_needs_plain: Moderate. Copes with poor soil but needs moisture until flowering.
records.rooting_notes: Fairly shallow roots; suits thin soils.
records.maturity_description: About three to four months from sowing.
why_it_may_fit: Grown on poor, acidic hill soils

records.title: Groundnut (peanut)
records.summary: A legume that tolerates mildly acidic soil, but needs loose, crumbly soil for its pods to form underground. Suits raised beds better than hard ground.
instructions: Grow only in loose, well-filled raised beds or containers; sow shelled seeds a finger-joint deep.
everyday_amounts: one or two shelled seeds per spot
about one finger-joint deep
limitations: Termites damage pods in dry soil.
Needs loose soil; gravel and crust stop pod formation.
No yield is promised.
safety_notes: Never eat mouldy groundnuts: moulds can be poisonous.
records.name: Groundnut

cautions.reason: Pegs cannot push into a hard crust; grow only in loose raised beds.
Needs loose soil depth for pods; only possible in well-filled raised beds.
Pods rot in waterlogged soil.
Needs steady moisture while flowering and filling pods.
Without organic matter, bed soil will be too hard and poor for pods.

records.water_needs_plain: Moderate. Needs moisture at flowering and pod filling.
records.rooting_notes: Pods develop underground on pegs; needs loose, crumbly soil, not gravel or crust.
records.maturity_description: About three to four months from sowing for bunch types.

records.title: Pigeon pea (tur)
records.summary: A long-season, deep-rooted shrubby legume. Drought-hardy once established, but slow and needs deeper soil than most of this plateau offers.
instructions: Sow only in the deepest pits, early in the rains; it can also act as a hedge and give stakes and fuel.
everyday_amounts: two or three seeds per pit
limitations: Usually too long for a short wet season on shallow soil; a trial only.
Pod borers are a major pest.
safety_notes: Cook dry seed thoroughly.
records.name: Pigeon pea

cautions.reason: Deep taproot cannot develop on a continuous rock sheet.
Needs deeper soil than a hand's depth; only the deepest pits.
Far too long to finish if rains are ending.
Long crop; likely to run into the dry period.
Long crop; very risky without knowing the season length.
Does not tolerate waterlogging.

records.water_needs_plain: Low once established; deep roots use moisture after rains end, where soil depth allows.
records.rooting_notes: Deep taproot; needs the deepest pockets or enlarged pits.
records.maturity_description: Short-duration types take around four to five months; local types much longer.
why_it_may_fit: Adds nitrogen; leaves feed the soil

records.title: Cashew (kaju)
records.summary: The classic tree crop of lateritic plateaus: tolerates acidic, poor, gravelly soil and long dry seasons, but needs a pocket of deeper soil for its roots.
instructions: Plant at the start of the rains in the deepest pocket or an enlarged pit filled with soil and compost.
Mulch widely and help with stored water in the first dry season.
Field crops can be grown between young trees for the first years.
limitations: Years before any harvest; does not solve this season's food needs.
Needs a pocket of deeper soil.
safety_notes: The raw nut shell contains a caustic liquid: never bite or crack raw nuts; they must be roasted or processed carefully.
records.name: Cashew

cautions.reason: Needs an enlarged pit in a crack or softer pocket; on solid rock it struggles.
Waterlogging kills cashew; plant only on raised, well-drained spots.
Young trees need watering in their first dry season.

records.water_needs_plain: Low once established; young trees need help through the first dry season.
records.rooting_notes: Deep taproot plus spreading roots; must have a pocket or enlarged pit of deeper soil.
records.maturity_description: Long-term: grafted trees may bear from about the third year; seedlings later. Full bearing takes several more years.
why_it_may_fit: Classic crop on lateritic, acidic ground

records.title: Mango (aam)
records.summary: A long-lived fruit tree that can grow on lateritic ground with an enlarged, well-filled pit, but needs more soil depth and early care than cashew.
instructions: Plant only where probing found a deep pocket; enlarge and fill the pit well before the rains.
limitations: Riskier than cashew on shallow laterite.
Years before fruit.
safety_notes: Mango sap can irritate skin; wash after handling cut stems.
records.name: Mango

cautions.reason: Needs real soil depth; a continuous rock sheet will not support it.
Only in an enlarged pit in the deepest pocket.
Young trees need watering through the first dry seasons.
Waterlogging harms roots.

records.water_needs_plain: Moderate while young; tolerant of dry seasons once deep-rooted.
records.rooting_notes: Deep taproot; needs the deepest pocket available.
records.maturity_description: Long-term: grafted trees may fruit after a few years; seedlings take longer.
why_it_may_fit: Tolerates a long dry season once established

records.title: Gliricidia (soil-building hedge)
records.summary: A fast nitrogen-fixing hedge tree grown from cuttings; its loppings are leafy mulch and green manure for pits and beds. Not a food crop.
instructions: Plant thick cuttings at the start of the rains along stone lines or bed edges.
Lop leafy branches and lay them on beds as mulch and green manure.
limitations: Not food: its value is soil-building, stakes and shade.
safety_notes: Do not eat any part. Seeds and bark are toxic; keep leaves as limited fodder only where local practice confirms.
records.name: Gliricidia

cautions.reason: Grows slower on solid rock; plant cuttings in cracks or at bed edges.

records.water_needs_plain: Low once rooted; cuttings need moist soil at planting.
records.rooting_notes: Roots find cracks in the hard layer; fairly tolerant of shallow soil.
records.maturity_description: Leaves can usually be lopped for mulch within about a year of planting cuttings.
why_it_may_fit: Builds soil fertility with its leaves
Strengthens stone lines as a living hedge

records.title: Amaranth greens (chaulai)
records.summary: The fastest food option: leafy amaranth grown in the richest pit or a small bed gives young leaves to pick within about a month, then keeps giving if picked often.
instructions: Mix the tiny seed with a few pinches of fine soil or sand so it scatters thinly, sprinkle it on a rich pit or bed and press it in; barely cover.
Thin to about a hand-span apart and eat the thinnings.
Pick the youngest leaves and tips often; pinch out flower heads to keep leaves coming.
everyday_amounts: a pinch of tiny seed mixed with fine soil per pit
thin to about a hand-span apart
limitations: Needs rich, fed soil; it is not a crop for bare laterite.
Leaves only; it does not store like grain unless dried.
No yield is promised.
safety_notes: Wash leaves in clean water and cook them; do not eat leaves sprayed with anything.
records.name: Amaranth greens

cautions.reason: Needs the richest pit or bed; on unfed laterite leaves stay small and tough.
Rots in waterlogged ground; use a raised bed.
Seedlings need the soil kept damp; plan only a small patch near stored water.

records.water_needs_plain: Moderate while small: keep the soil damp until plants are a hand tall, then rain and mulch are usually enough.
records.rooting_notes: Shallow, fine roots: well suited to a rich pit or a shallow bed.
records.maturity_description: First young leaves can usually be picked about four to six weeks after sowing; picking can continue for several weeks if flowering is delayed.
why_it_may_fit: Fastest food: first leaves in about a month
Very useful when the season length is unknown or short
Tolerates acidic soil better than many vegetables
Needs only a small rich pit or bed

records.title: Sorghum (jowar)
records.summary: A drought-tough grain that can stay green through dry spells when other cereals fail. Less tolerant of strong acidity than finger millet, so treat it as a trial crop here.
instructions: Sow a pinch of seeds about one finger-joint deep in each pit early in the reliable rains; thin to the strongest two or three plants.
Do not crowd: crowded sorghum suffers most in dry spells.
everyday_amounts: a pinch of a few seeds per planting spot
sow about one finger-joint deep
limitations: Less suited to strong acidity than finger millet; compare in a trial.
Birds and striga are serious problems.
No yield is promised.
safety_notes: Check seed is not chemically treated before eating any of it.
records.name: Sorghum

cautions.reason: Needs roughly three to four and a half months; too long if rains are ending.
Longer than pearl millet; risky when the season length is not known.
Roots want more depth than a rock sheet allows; only in well-filled raised beds.
A weak hint of acidity: sorghum copes less well with acidic soil than finger millet.

records.water_needs_plain: Low once established; tolerates dry spells well, especially after flowering.
records.rooting_notes: Strong, fairly deep roots; does best in the deeper pits and beds.
records.maturity_description: About three to four and a half months from sowing, depending on the type.

records.title: Sweet potato (shakarkand)
records.summary: Grown from vine cuttings on mounds or raised beds; tolerates acidic soil, covers the ground like a living mulch, and gives storable roots.
instructions: Plant cuttings about a forearm long, burying a few leaf joints in a mound or raised bed with the tip out.
Use only moderate compost: very rich soil gives vines and few roots.
Pile soil over any cracks around the mound as roots swell, to keep weevils out.
everyday_amounts: cuttings about a forearm long
a few leaf joints buried per cutting
limitations: Needs loose soil depth in a mound or bed.
Weevils and rats damage roots.
No yield is promised.
safety_notes: Cook roots before eating.
records.name: Sweet potato

cautions.reason: Roots need loose soil depth; only in tall, well-filled raised beds or mounds.
Needs a mound or raised bed; flat shallow ground gives vines but few roots.
Roots rot in waterlogged soil.
Water sitting on the hard layer rots roots; raise mounds higher.
Cuttings need damp soil for their first weeks.
Needs several wet weeks to root and bulk up.

records.water_needs_plain: Needs damp soil for the first few weeks while cuttings root; fairly drought-tolerant once established.
records.rooting_notes: Storage roots form in loose soil above the hard layer; needs a mound or raised bed.
records.maturity_description: Roughly three and a half to five months from planting cuttings.
why_it_may_fit: Vines cover and shade the ground

records.title: Cassava (tapioca)
records.summary: A very long-season root that is highly tolerant of acidic, infertile soil and survives the dry season in the ground; it needs loose mounds or pockets and careful processing before eating.
instructions: Plant stem pieces about a forearm long from healthy plants, about two-thirds buried at a slant in a tall mound, buds pointing up.
Plant early in the reliable rains so roots establish before the dry season.
Mulch the mound and keep weeds down while plants are small; on slopes, plant behind stone lines because young cassava leaves soil bare.
everyday_amounts: stem pieces about a forearm long
about two-thirds buried
limitations: Far longer than one wet season; it does not feed you this season.
Needs loose pockets or mounds.
Leaves little ground cover when young, so soil can wash on slopes.
No yield is promised.
safety_notes: Never eat cassava raw. Roots and leaves contain natural poisons: peel, soak and cook thoroughly using the locally known safe method.
Use only cuttings from healthy plants to avoid spreading mosaic disease.
records.name: Cassava

cautions.reason: Roots need loose pockets or tall mounds; on a continuous rock sheet they stay small or rot.
Only in tall mounds or the deepest pits.
Roots rot in waterlogged soil.
Water sitting on the hard layer rots roots.
Cuttings need several wet weeks to root before the dry season.

records.water_needs_plain: Low once established; survives the long dry season in the ground.
records.rooting_notes: Thick storage roots need loose soil; plant in tall mounds or enlarged pits.
records.maturity_description: Long-term: roughly eight months to a year before roots are worth digging; they can then be left in the ground and dug as needed.
why_it_may_fit: Highly tolerant of acidic, infertile soil
Survives the dry season and stores in the ground

records.title: Pineapple (long-term perennial) (ananas)
records.summary: An optional long-term perennial with shallow roots that tolerates acidic soil and dry months; grown from leafy tops or slips in rich pits or stone-edged beds. Fruit takes well over a year.
instructions: Twist the leafy top off a ripe fruit, let the cut end dry for a few days, then push it into a rich pit or bed early in the rains.
Mulch around it and keep the base free of standing water.
limitations: Very slow: a long-term option only.
Optional; not a staple food.
safety_notes: Leaves are spiny at the edges; wear something on your hands.
records.name: Pineapple (long-term perennial)

cautions.reason: Rots in standing water.
Plant only on raised, well-drained spots.
Needs a rich planting pocket to grow at a useful pace.

records.water_needs_plain: Low once rooted; stores water in its leaves.
records.rooting_notes: Shallow roots: suits a hand's depth of rich soil in pits or stone beds.
records.maturity_description: Long-term: usually around one and a half to two years from planting a top or slip to the first fruit.
why_it_may_fit: Planting material comes from a fruit top

records.title: Neem tree (neem)
records.summary: A hardy shade tree for poor, dry ground whose leaves are used for a mild pest wash and dry-store protection; long-term, not a food crop.
instructions: Plant a seedling early in the reliable rains in an enlarged pit with a basin and mulch ring.
Protect it from goats and other browsing animals with thorny branches.
limitations: Not food.
Slow to give much shade.
safety_notes: Neem oil and seed are not food: keep extracts away from children and never swallow them.
records.name: Neem tree

cautions.reason: Plant in a crack or the deepest pocket; growth is slow on solid rock.
Dislikes waterlogged ground.

records.water_needs_plain: Low after the first dry season.
records.rooting_notes: Deep roots find cracks in the hard layer over time.
records.maturity_description: Long-term: leaves can be gathered lightly within about a year; shade and seed take several years.
why_it_may_fit: Leaves for pest washes and grain stores
Shade and fuel in later years

records.title: Moringa (drumstick tree)
records.summary: A fast tree grown from cuttings or seed whose young leaves and tender pods are eaten; copes with dry, poor soil but hates waterlogging.
instructions: Push a thick cutting about a forearm long into a filled pit early in the rains, or sow seed in a rich pit.
Prune the top often so leaves stay within reach.
limitations: Hates waterlogging.
Leaves are a supplement, not a staple.
safety_notes: Eat only leaves, flowers and pods; cook pods and leaves.
records.name: Moringa

cautions.reason: Roots rot in waterlogged ground.
Plant only where water drains away.
Needs a pocket of deeper soil; stays small on solid rock.

records.water_needs_plain: Low after establishment; water young plants in the first dry season.
records.rooting_notes: Thick taproot; plant in the deepest well-drained pocket.
records.maturity_description: Leaves can usually be picked from about six months after planting; pods later.

records.title: Sunn hemp (green manure) (san)
records.summary: A fast nitrogen-fixing green manure sown in spare beds or between stone lines and cut at flowering to feed the soil. Not food.
instructions: Scatter seed thickly in spare beds or between stone lines early in the rains and cover lightly.
Cut as flowers appear and lay the cut plants on beds or mix them into pits.
limitations: Not food: it uses space and water that a food crop could use; grow it in spare beds.
safety_notes: Do not eat the seeds or feed them to animals; they can be poisonous.
records.name: Sunn hemp (green manure)

cautions.reason: Grows poorly in standing water.

records.water_needs_plain: Rain only.
records.rooting_notes: Taproot; grows in shallow beds.
records.maturity_description: Usually ready to cut for green manure about six to nine weeks after sowing, as the first flowers open.
why_it_may_fit: Adds nitrogen and green matter quickly

records.title: Grass hedge (vetiver or local clump grass) (khus)
records.summary: A tight line of clump grass planted along the uphill side of stone lines to hold soil and slow runoff; trimmed for mulch. Not food.
instructions: Split clumps into slips and plant them about a hand-span apart in a tight line along the uphill side of a stone line.
Fill any gap in the line; water finds gaps.
limitations: Not food.
Use a non-spreading clump grass known locally; avoid grasses that spread into beds.
safety_notes: Do not burn the hedge; dry grass fires spread fast.
records.name: Grass hedge (vetiver or local clump grass)

cautions.reason: On flat ground there is little runoff to slow; use it only along bed edges or drains.

records.water_needs_plain: Rain only once rooted.
records.rooting_notes: Dense roots bind the soil of stone lines and bed edges.
records.maturity_description: Forms a useful hedge over roughly half a year to a year; trim for mulch once it is dense.
